function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Sure thing! Here are a few ways you can get a cake delivered (or pick one up) depending on what you’re looking for:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips |
|--------|----------------|--------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, custom‑made cakes, often with a personal touch | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, call or visit the bakery’s website | Ask about delivery times, pickup windows, and any special dietary requests (gluten‑free, vegan, etc.) |
| **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide or regional delivery, often with a wide variety of flavors and designs | Sites like **Goldbelly**, **Bakeology**, **Cake Delivery**, **Etsy** (for custom orders) | Check delivery fees, shipping times, and whether the cake is shipped in a temperature‑controlled container. |
| **Grocery stores & supermarkets** | Ready‑made cakes, sometimes with delivery via their own service or through third‑party apps | Many chains (Whole Foods, Kroger, Safeway, Publix) offer online ordering with curbside pickup or delivery | Great for quick orders; check if they have a “specialty” or “artisan” section for higher‑quality cakes. |
| **Specialty dessert shops** | Unique flavors, artisanal or gourmet cakes | Look for local patisseries or specialty dessert shops; many now offer online ordering | Ideal if you want something a bit more upscale or niche (e.g., French macarons, Japanese matcha cakes). |
| **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (often themed) | Services like **Baker’s Dozen**, **Cakes & Co.**, or **Dessert Club** | Fun for regular treats or gifting; check the subscription terms and cancellation policy. |
| **DIY kits** | All the ingredients and instructions delivered | Brands like **Bakeology**, **Kraft**, or **Amazon** sell cake‑making kits | Great if you want to bake at home but still enjoy a “ready‑to‑make” cake. |

### Quick steps to place an order

1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, anniversary, corporate event, etc.) and any dietary restrictions.
2. **Choose a style** (classic vanilla, chocolate, red velvet, custom design, etc.).
3. **Pick a vendor**: local bakery for freshness, online service for convenience, or grocery store for speed.
4. **Place the order**: most sites let you specify delivery date/time, address, and any special instructions.
5. **Confirm payment**: credit card, PayPal, or sometimes cash on delivery.
6. **Track the order**: many services provide a tracking number or delivery window.

### If you’re in a specific city

If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated local bakeries or delivery services that operate in your area. Just let me know!
